claims.text: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the driver must carry limb (c) on its own words: he must have 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' the 300 seconds the fee schedule sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The driver's own 10-second telemetry records exactly two in-geofence holds, 170 seconds from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds from 18:49:35, each reported as a separate run. The longest continuous hold anywhere in this pickup is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short of the minimum, and the rider's description of a car that 'kept moving around' and never 'stayed 5 minutes in one place' is precisely what the trace records.

The only route by which the driver reaches 300 seconds is the summing of the two holds permitted by POL-NS-06(i), and that permission is conditional: the trace must show the driver leaving and re-entering the arrival radius 'without at any point travelling more than 300 m from the pin'. Over this pickup (18:39:05 to 18:52:40) the trace summary reports a maximum distance from the pin of 1,191.8 m - some four times the leash - and a total track of 3.0 km. The smaller 179.0 m figure reported for the inter-interval excursion is not the driver's maximum range on the trace. If the leash is applied to the trace as its words 'at any point' require, the condition for accumulation is not made out, the intervals cannot be summed, and the effective dwell remains the single 185-second hold.

Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the POL-NS-02 geofence at or before the timestamp of the arrival event. The event is logged at 18:44:30, while the earliest qualifying in-radius fix on the driver's own trace opens the first qualifying run at 18:44:45 - fifteen seconds later, and more than one 10-second sampling interval behind the marker. The record therefore carries no admissible in-radius fix at or before the marker to support the condition that marker certifies, and the waiting clock under POL-NS-01(c) runs from the first qualifying fix at 18:44:45, not from the marker.

trip_record.wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is not dwell: it is elapsed time from the 18:44:30 marker to the 18:52:45 cancellation, 495 seconds in all. Across that period the trace accounts for only 355 seconds inside the arrival radius; the balancing 140 seconds is time outside the geofence, including the 120-second loop between 18:47:35 and 18:49:35 during which the driver reached 179 m from the pin and speeds of up to 49.6 km/h. A 'wait' figure built on the marker cannot supply the continuous 300-second hold POL-NS-01(c) requires.

The rider does not press POL-NS-04, and says so plainly rather than stretching it: her 18:46:20 message was followed by the driver's 18:47:50 reply, ninety seconds later, so limb (b)'s 120-second-silence requirement is not met and the clause cannot run in her favour. This case is decided on the dwell arithmetic under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06, not on the contact clause.

The contested sum is the cancellation-fee line alone. fare_breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Where the effective dwell falls short of the POL-NS-01 minimum for the zone class, POL-NS-06 refunds that line to the rider in full and states that no driver compensation is payable. The rider seeks SGD 4.00 returned and no compensation paid out of it; the fee is the only amount the ledger moved.

claims.text: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-08-07T18:44:30, and the GPS trace then places the driver inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius of 120 m from 18:44:45, generating 40 qualifying in-radius fixes across two separate holds (18:44:45-18:47:35 and 18:49:35-18:52:40). That is far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires before arrival is deemed established, so POL-NS-01 limb (a) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are both satisfied on the trace's own numbers.

There is no false arrival marker to attack. Nothing in the record places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h or above at the 18:44:30 marker: the derived excursion block measures the driver's furthest point between the two holds at 178.95 m, and it records the POL-NS-06(i) limb as available rather than flagging any false-arrival condition. Even on the rider's best case that the marker preceded the first in-radius fix by a single 10 second sampling interval, POL-NS-05(iii) applies: the waiting clock is recomputed to the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45, and because the corrected dwell still exceeds the 300 second minimum the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 355 accumulated seconds - two holds of 170 s and 185 s - against the LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 s. The derived shortfall is minus 55 seconds, meaning there is no shortfall at all, so POL-NS-06 returns no refund. The rider's assertion that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' misdescribes the test: the required dwell need not be served in one place, because POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed toward the 300 second minimum.

Accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) is available on this record because EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION: an LTA DataMall full-day bus lane on Orchard Road and Orchard Turn in force 17:00-20:00, with TrafficMarshals and enforcement cameras active, whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the whole 18:38-18:52 trip window. The limb's distance qualification is met too - the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 178.95 m, inside the 300 m leash. The trace's larger whole-run maximum of 1191.8 m is not a position inside either in-geofence hold (a hold is by definition within 120 m of the pin) but a start-of-trace approach figure, the trace opening at 18:39:05, five minutes before the 18:44:30 arrival.

The driver's own chat account of why he moved - that the marshal made him move because the bus lane runs until 8pm, and that he told the rider he was going one round and coming back to the same place - is corroborated by the LTA advisory for exactly that road and window, and the trace matches it fix for fix: he leaves the geofence at 18:47:35 and is back inside it at 18:49:35, a 120 second loop whose furthest point is 178.95 m from the pin, followed by a further 185 second hold. That is a driver complying with a no-stopping kerb, which is the very situation POL-NS-06(i) was drafted to cover, not a driver abandoning the pickup.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on the trip record's own fields: the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, five seconds after the last qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:52:40, and there is no boarding event anywhere in the record - started_at and ended_at are both null. RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes the limb recognises, and the recorded wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is consistent with the 18:44:30 arrival marker and the 18:52:45 cancellation.

The rider's own track places her device between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pickup pin across all 70 fixes in the waiting window, at zero speed throughout, and the qualifying rider fix count against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius is nil. She was not at the pickup and not approaching it at any moment before cancellation. That answers 'I was coming down for you' and removes limb (c) of POL-NS-04 from the case: the rider-exoneration route cannot be run on this trace.

Independently of presence, POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver answered inside the 120 second window: the rider's 'ok coming down now' was sent at 18:46:20 and the driver's reply - that the marshal had moved him and he was going one round and returning to the same place - was sent at 18:47:50, 90 seconds later. Limb (b) therefore fails, and any residual coordination question is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06 rather than by exonerating the rider.

POL-NS-03 has no purchase on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary for the required dwell outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's two stationary holds are inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius at a pickup with a single registered point (venue_id VEN-ION-ORCHARD, registered_pickup_points 1), so no wrong-entrance, wrong-block or pin-ambiguity case arises and no goodwill payment is in issue.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is compensated at 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, that is SGD 3.20, under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, below the threshold of 0.08. The clause requires both limbs and neither is met, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The SGD 4.00 actually charged reconciles under POL-NS-08(d): it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00, the two dimensions agreeing, so there is no fare defect and no basis for splitting the fee. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the correct disposition of the contested amount is that the present charge stands, with the SGD 3.20 driver payment recorded as an independent, platform-funded figure per POL-GEN-03 and never netted against the rider's fee.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged, so this case is decidable on the record and the fee should not be placed on hold. The two admissible traces agree rather than contradict (arrival 18:44:30, cancellation 18:52:45, 8.3 minutes); every one of the seven artifacts in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence; the parties share no other no-show dispute in the trailing 90 days, both disputes_with_counterparty_90d being 0; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: the $4.00 cancellation fee stands and the driver is paid $3.20 (80% of the fee; the remaining 20% is retained as the platform service fee).

To the RIDER. Your dispute does not succeed, and the reasons are arithmetic. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and needs four things: a driver 'arrived' event, GPS placing the driver inside the pickup geofence around that event, a position held for at least the 300 seconds the fee schedule sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and a driver-side termination carrying a recognised no-show reason code. The driver's own 10-second GPS trace (EV-GPS-00214) records two in-geofence holds at the ION Orchard PHV bay: 18:44:45-18:47:35 (170 s) and 18:49:35-18:52:40 (185 s), 355 seconds in total, 55 seconds more than the minimum. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00214) shows the 'arrived' event at 18:44:30 and a driver cancellation at 18:52:45 coded RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event. Your description of a car that 'kept moving around' and 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' is accurate as a description but it is not the test: POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals inside one pickup attempt to be added together, and the LTA bus-lane restriction on Orchard Road/Orchard Turn (EV-ADVIS-00214-01, in force 17:00-20:00, marshals and cameras active, geometry covering the pickup bay) is precisely the situation that limb was written for. The $4.00 charged reconciles with the fee schedule, being the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) raises no billing defect.

Your three remaining arguments are answered. (1) The 1,191.8 m maximum on the trace is the driver's approach to the bay from 18:39:05, before the pickup attempt began; the 300 m leash in POL-NS-06(i) governs the leaving and re-entering between the two holds, where the computed maximum was 178.95 m - comfortably inside it. (2) The arrival marker at 18:44:30 precedes the first in-radius fix at 18:44:45 by one 10-second sampling interval. That is not a false arrival marker: POL-NS-05 fires only where the marker places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more, and neither is met. In any case POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the marker, so those 15 seconds do not count against the driver either way. (3) You are right that the 8.3-minute wait_time_min is elapsed time and not dwell; the dwell that decides this case is the 355 seconds the trace records, and that is over the minimum.

You did not press POL-NS-04, and correctly so: the driver replied to your 18:46:20 message at 18:47:50, within the 120-second window, so the clause cannot run. Your own device's GPS fixes place you roughly 690-717 m from the pickup pin, stationary, for the entire waiting window, with no qualifying fix inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius - so the no-show termination reflected a genuine no-show.

To the DRIVER. Your account is accepted. You were at the bay, you were moved on by the marshal because of the bus lane, you said in the chat (18:47:50) that you were going one round and returning to the same place, and you were back inside the geofence by 18:49:35. The trace matches your account and the LTA advisory for that road and window. Because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, POL-NS-07 gives you compensation of 80% of the $4.00 fee, i.e. $3.20. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2 / 118 completed trips is 0.017 (below 0.08) - and POL-NS-07 requires both limbs. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 applies: the holds are inside the 120 m arrival radius at a pickup with a single registered point, so there is no wrong-entrance or pin-ambiguity case; there is no waiting-period shortfall; and there is no false arrival marker.

On the evidence: all seven artifacts in the bundle are COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so nothing is discounted and the confidence cap is not reduced. Only the profile fields the policy names were used - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d for the POL-NS-07 check, and no_show_disputes_30d and the counterparty-dispute counters for POL-NS-09; every other profile field is context only and carried no weight. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged: the artifacts agree rather than contradict, no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence, the parties share no other trailing-90-day no-show dispute, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no_show_disputes_30d is 1. No clause in this case produces a referral, so none is issued. Per POL-GEN-03, on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's charge itself stands unchanged.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, here is the decision. The $4.00 no-show fee stands, and the driver is paid $3.20 compensation.

Why the fee stands. A no-show fee is chargeable only if the driver waited the required 5 minutes (300 seconds) inside the pickup area at ION Orchard, a LARGE_VENUE zone. The driver's own GPS, sampled every 10 seconds with no gaps, shows two holds at the bay: 170 seconds from 6:44:45pm and 185 seconds from 6:49:35pm. The rider is right that the driver never stayed 5 minutes in one place — the longest single hold is 185 seconds. But POL-NS-06(i) lets separate holds be added together where holding the kerb was not lawfully possible and the driver stayed within 300 m of the pin throughout. Both conditions hold: the LTA DataMall advisory shows a full-day bus lane on Orchard Turn in force until 8pm with marshals and cameras active, and the driver's loop away from the bay stayed 179 m from the pin. Added up, the in-area wait is 355 seconds — 55 seconds more than the 300 required, so there is no shortfall to refund.

The 1,191 m maximum distance the rider points to is the driver's position at the start of the trace, five minutes before he reached Orchard — his approach to the pickup, not movement during the wait. The 300 m leash in POL-NS-06(i) applies to the leave-and-return loop between the two holds, which was 179 m. The 8.3-minute figure in the trip record is elapsed time, not dwell; the dwell the policy measures is the 355 seconds actually spent inside the pickup area, and it is enough.

The arrival tap at 6:44:30pm preceded the first qualifying in-area fix by one 10-second interval. The policy measures the waiting clock from the first qualifying fix, not the tap, and an early tap while pulling into the pickup road is sloppy but does not by itself void the fee where the driver then genuinely waited the full period; it did not void it here. Nor is this a false-arrival case: at the marker the driver was not more than 300 m from the pin and not travelling at 15 km/h or more.

The rider's contact-clause argument does not run either. We agree POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied to the rider's 6:46:20pm message at 6:47:50pm, 90 seconds later and inside the 120-second window, and the rider's own device sits between 690 m and 717 m from the pickup throughout, so the presence limb fails as well. The $4.00 charge matches the fee schedule exactly — the greater of the $4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone fee and the $4.00 RYDE_X tier fee — so no part of it is refundable on integrity grounds.

Why the driver is paid. The fee is properly chargeable and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, so the driver receives 80% of the fee, $3.20, with the remaining 20% retained as the platform fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: 2 no-show terminations in 30 days (below the threshold of 4) and a rate of 0.017 (below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld. The rider's $4.00 charge is not netted against this; the $3.20 is a separate driver payment.

No escalation. The trip record and the GPS agree on arrival and termination, every artifact in the bundle is complete at full weight, and no repeat-dispute or abuse trigger is met, so nothing is held for review. The driver's account in the chat — that the marshal moved him on because of the bus lane and that he went one round and came straight back — matches the LTA advisory and the trace fix for fix, which is why this fee is upheld.

We agree POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied to the rider's 6:46:20pm message at 6:47:50pm, 90 seconds later and inside the 120-second window, and the rider's own device sits between 690 m and 717 m from the pickup throughout, so the presence limb fails as well. The $4.00 charge matches the fee schedule exactly — the greater of the $4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone fee and the $4.00 RYDE_X tier fee — so no part of it is refundable on integrity grounds.

Why the driver is paid. The fee is properly chargeable and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, so the driver receives 80% of the fee, $3.20, with the remaining 20% retained as the platform fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: 2 no-show terminations in 30 days (below the threshold of 4) and a rate of 0.017 (below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld. The rider's $4.00 charge is not netted against this; the $3.20 is a separate driver payment.

No escalation. The trip record and the GPS agree on arrival and termination, every artifact in the bundle is complete at full weight, and no repeat-dispute or abuse trigger is met, so nothing is held for review. The driver's account in the chat — that the marshal moved him on because of the bus lane and that he went one round and came straight back — matches the LTA advisory and the trace fix for fix, which is why this fee is upheld."},"discarded_claims":[]}

ruling.explanation:
Driver, the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee stands and you are owed SGD 3.20 (80% of it, the platform keeping the other 20%). Rider, your dispute is not upheld and the SGD 4.00 charge remains as it is.

Why the four POL-NS-01 conditions hold. (a) The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 18:44:30. (b) The GPS trace places the car at the ION Orchard bay with 40 qualifying in-radius fixes; the first, at 18:44:45, is one 10-second sample after the marker. The marker fired as the car was turning into the pickup road — the sloppy-but-harmless case POL-NS-05 describes — and because the wait then served meets the minimum, the marker does not defeat the fee. Rider, your point that no in-radius fix appears at or before 18:44:30 is noted, but the trace still establishes the car at the bay and the marker is out by less than one sampling interval. (c) The waiting requirement is met. The trace shows two stationary holds inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius — 170 seconds from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds from 18:49:35 — 355 seconds in total, 55 seconds ahead of the 300-second minimum. Rider, you are right that the car never held still for five continuous minutes and that the longest single hold was 185 seconds; but POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits the separate in-geofence intervals of one pickup attempt to be added, and its conditions are satisfied: EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is a KERB_RESTRICTION (full-day bus lane on Orchard Road/Orchard Turn, 17:00-20:00, marshals and enforcement active) whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose window covers the whole wait, so holding the kerb was not lawfully possible; and the furthest point between the holds was 179 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. The 1,191.8 m trace maximum is the distance from where the car began its approach at 18:39:05, before it reached the bay — not ground covered while circling — so it does not disqualify the summing. (d) The trip was ended by the driver at 18:52:45 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event occurred.

Rider, the routes that could have refunded you fail. POL-NS-04 needs the driver to leave your message unanswered for 120 seconds; you wrote at 18:46:20 and he replied at 18:47:50, ninety seconds later, explaining the marshal had moved him and that he was going one round and returning to the same place. You do not press the clause yourself, and on the trace your device sat 690-717 m from the pickup at zero speed throughout, so its presence limb would not have run either. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the car's stationary holds were inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong entrance.

No escalation applies. All seven artifacts are complete at full weight (1.0), the two traces agree with each other and with the trip record, the anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations against 118 completed trips, below both thresholds), and there is no repeat-dispute pattern between you. The fee therefore stands, and the driver is compensated as above.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your complaint is that the driver never stayed five minutes in one place and kept moving, and the trace does bear you out that he never held still continuously for five minutes — his two stationary holds inside the pickup radius lasted 170 seconds and 185 seconds. But the 300-second waiting period a LARGE_VENUE pickup requires may be counted across more than one hold where the driver is being moved on by a lawful kerbside restriction, and that is what the record shows here. An LTA advisory for Orchard Road and Orchard Turn (full-day bus lane 17:00-20:00, enforcement cameras and marshals active) covered the pickup road for the whole of this pickup, and the driver's loop away from and back to the bay never took him further than 179 m from the pin, well inside the 300 m limit. The two holds add to 355 seconds, so the 300-second minimum is met and your $4.00 cancellation fee stands. The 1,191.8 m figure in the trace is the distance he covered bringing the car to the pickup before he arrived, not a position during the wait, so it does not break the accumulation rule, and the 179 m figure is the one that measures the loop. His '8.3 minutes' wait figure is elapsed time, not dwell, and I have not relied on it. I also cannot run the rider-exoneration route your advocate fairly declined to press: the driver answered your 'ok coming down now' message 90 seconds later, inside the 120-second window, and your device never came inside the pickup presence radius at any point, so that route fails on its own terms. The arrival marker at 18:44:30 sits at most one 10-second sampling interval ahead of the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45; the waiting clock runs from that fix rather than the marker, and on the recomputed basis the accumulated dwell still exceeds the minimum, so the marker does not defeat the fee. To the driver: your fee is upheld and you are paid SGD 3.20, being 80 per cent of the $4.00 fee, with the remaining 20 per cent retained as the platform service fee. The 'amount' figure carried alongside is the same SGD 3.20, not a second payment and not a refund to the rider, whose charge stands. Your profile does not trip the anti-farming check — 2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days, below the threshold of 4, and 2 of 118 completed trips, 1.7 per cent, below the threshold of 8 per cent — so compensation is paid rather than withheld. The wrong-entrance and pin-ambiguity clause has no purchase: the pickup is a single registered point inside the arrival radius, so no goodwill payment arises. The $4.00 charged reconciles with the fee schedule as the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), which agree, so there is no fare defect. Every artifact in the bundle is complete at full weight, the traces agree rather than contradict, neither party shows a repeat no-show dispute with the other in the trailing 90 days, and the rider's 30-day no-show dispute count is 1, so no escalation trigger is engaged and the fee is not placed on hold. No clause directs a referral, so none is made.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the driver must carry limb (c) on its own words: he must have 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' the 300 seconds the fee schedule sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The driver's own 10-second telemetry records exactly two in-geofence holds, 170 seconds from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds from 18:49:35, each reported as a separate run. The longest continuous hold anywhere in this pickup is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short of the minimum, and the rider's description of a car that 'kept moving around' and never 'stayed 5 minutes in one place' is precisely what the trace records.

The only route by which the driver reaches 300 seconds is the summing of the two holds permitted by POL-NS-06(i), and that permission is conditional: the trace must show the driver leaving and re-entering the arrival radius 'without at any point travelling more than 300 m from the pin'. Over this pickup (18:39:05 to 18:52:40) the trace summary reports a maximum distance from the pin of 1,191.8 m - some four times the leash - and a total track of 3.0 km. The smaller 179.0 m figure reported for the inter-interval excursion is not the driver's maximum range on the trace. If the leash is applied to the trace as its words 'at any point' require, the condition for accumulation is not made out, the intervals cannot be summed, and the effective dwell remains the single 185-second hold.

Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the POL-NS-02 geofence at or before the timestamp of the arrival event. The event is logged at 18:44:30, while the earliest qualifying in-radius fix on the driver's own trace opens the first qualifying run at 18:44:45 - fifteen seconds later, and more than one 10-second sampling interval behind the marker. The record therefore carries no admissible in-radius fix at or before the marker to support the condition that marker certifies, and the waiting clock under POL-NS-01(c) runs from the first qualifying fix at 18:44:45, not from the marker.

trip_record.wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is not dwell: it is elapsed time from the 18:44:30 marker to the 18:52:45 cancellation, 495 seconds in all. Across that period the trace accounts for only 355 seconds inside the arrival radius; the balancing 140 seconds is time outside the geofence, including the 120-second loop between 18:47:35 and 18:49:35 during which the driver reached 179 m from the pin and speeds of up to 49.6 km/h. A 'wait' figure built on the marker cannot supply the continuous 300-second hold POL-NS-01(c) requires.

The rider does not press POL-NS-04, and says so plainly rather than stretching it: her 18:46:20 message was followed by the driver's 18:47:50 reply, ninety seconds later, so limb (b)'s 120-second-silence requirement is not met and the clause cannot run in her favour. This case is decided on the dwell arithmetic under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06, not on the contact clause.

The contested sum is the cancellation-fee line alone. fare_breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Where the effective dwell falls short of the POL-NS-01 minimum for the zone class, POL-NS-06 refunds that line to the rider in full and states that no driver compensation is payable. The rider seeks SGD 4.00 returned and no compensation paid out of it; the fee is the only amount the ledger moved.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-08-07T18:44:30, and the GPS trace then places the driver inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius of 120 m from 18:44:45, generating 40 qualifying in-radius fixes across two separate holds (18:44:45-18:47:35 and 18:49:35-18:52:40). That is far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires before arrival is deemed established, so POL-NS-01 limb (a) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are both satisfied on the trace's own numbers.

There is no false arrival marker to attack. Nothing in the record places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h or above at the 18:44:30 marker: the derived excursion block measures the driver's furthest point between the two holds at 178.95 m, and it records the POL-NS-06(i) limb as available rather than flagging any false-arrival condition. Even on the rider's best case that the marker preceded the first in-radius fix by a single 10 second sampling interval, POL-NS-05(iii) applies: the waiting clock is recomputed to the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45, and because the corrected dwell still exceeds the 300 second minimum the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 355 accumulated seconds - two holds of 170 s and 185 s - against the LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 s. The derived shortfall is minus 55 seconds, meaning there is no shortfall at all, so POL-NS-06 returns no refund. The rider's assertion that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' misdescribes the test: the required dwell need not be served in one place, because POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed toward the 300 second minimum.

Accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) is available on this record because EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION: an LTA DataMall full-day bus lane on Orchard Road and Orchard Turn in force 17:00-20:00, with TrafficMarshals and enforcement cameras active, whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the whole 18:38-18:52 trip window. The limb's distance qualification is met too - the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 178.95 m, inside the 300 m leash. The trace's larger whole-run maximum of 1191.8 m is not a position inside either in-geofence hold (a hold is by definition within 120 m of the pin) but a start-of-trace approach figure, the trace opening at 18:39:05, five minutes before the 18:44:30 arrival.

The driver's own chat account of why he moved - that the marshal made him move because the bus lane runs until 8pm, and that he told the rider he was going one round and coming back to the same place - is corroborated by the LTA advisory for exactly that road and window, and the trace matches it fix for fix: he leaves the geofence at 18:47:35 and is back inside it at 18:49:35, a 120 second loop whose furthest point is 178.95 m from the pin, followed by a further 185 second hold. That is a driver complying with a no-stopping kerb, which is the very situation POL-NS-06(i) was drafted to cover, not a driver abandoning the pickup.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on the trip record's own fields: the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, five seconds after the last qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:52:40, and there is no boarding event anywhere in the record - started_at and ended_at are both null. RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes the limb recognises, and the recorded wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is consistent with the 18:44:30 arrival marker and the 18:52:45 cancellation.

The rider's own track places her device between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pickup pin across all 70 fixes in the waiting window, at zero speed throughout, and the qualifying rider fix count against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius is nil. She was not at the pickup and not approaching it at any moment before cancellation. That answers 'I was coming down for you' and removes limb (c) of POL-NS-04 from the case: the rider-exoneration route cannot be run on this trace.

Independently of presence, POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver answered inside the 120 second window: the rider's 'ok coming down now' was sent at 18:46:20 and the driver's reply - that the marshal had moved him and he was going one round and returning to the same place - was sent at 18:47:50, 90 seconds later. Limb (b) therefore fails, and any residual coordination question is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06 rather than by exonerating the rider.

POL-NS-03 has no purchase on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary for the required dwell outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's two stationary holds are inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius at a pickup with a single registered point (venue_id VEN-ION-ORCHARD, registered_pickup_points 1), so no wrong-entrance, wrong-block or pin-ambiguity case arises and no goodwill payment is in issue.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is compensated at 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, that is SGD 3.20, under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, below the threshold of 0.08. The clause requires both limbs and neither is met, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The SGD 4.00 actually charged reconciles under POL-NS-08(d): it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00, the two dimensions agreeing, so there is no fare defect and no basis for splitting the fee. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the correct disposition of the contested amount is that the present charge stands, with the SGD 3.20 driver payment recorded as an independent, platform-funded figure per POL-GEN-03 and never netted against the rider's fee.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged, so this case is decidable on the record and the fee should not be placed on hold. The two admissible traces agree rather than contradict (arrival 18:44:30, cancellation 18:52:45, 8.3 minutes); every one of the seven artifacts in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence; the parties share no other no-show dispute in the trailing 90 days, both disputes_with_counterparty_90d being 0; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3.
